Rashi on Pesachim 78b:10:1.hebrew: יוצאין בפסח אחד - ואע"פ שאין בו כזית לכל אחד, אלמא אכילה לא מעכבא:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:10:1.english: Fulfill [their obligation] with one Paschal lamb - Even though there is not an olive-bulk in it for each one; thus, eating is not indispensable.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:11:1.hebrew: דאי מימשכי הני - מה שיש בהן יותר מכזית לכל אחד, חזי להני הנשארים:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:11:1.english: As, if these withdraw - Whatever there is among them [amounting to] more than an olive-bulk for each one is fit for these remaining ones.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:11:2.hebrew: ואי מימשכי הני כו' - אישתכח דחזי לכולהו, דהי מינייהו מפקת? הלכך, אע"ג דלא אימשיך חד מינייהו, פטורין; אבל ניטמא, לא חזי אפילו לחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:11:2.english: And if these withdraw, etc. - It turns out that it is fit for all of them, for which of them would you exclude? Therefore, even though not one of them withdrew, they are exempt; but [if] it became impure, it is not fit even for one [person].

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:12:1.english: Registered for it - until there was an olive-bulk for each one.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:15:1.hebrew: ומאי דוחקיה דרב - לאוקמא למתני' כר' נתן דלא מעכבא, ולמימרא דמתני' לכתחילה קאמר, הא אם זרק הורצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:15:1.english: And what compelled Rav - to establish the Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Natan, [holding] that it is not indispensable, and to say that the Mishnah is speaking ab initio, whereas if he [already] sprinkled [the blood], it is accepted?

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:15:2.hebrew: נוקמה כרבנן - ונימא דמתני' אפי' בדיעבד פסול:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:15:2.english: Let us establish it in accordance with the Rabbis - And let us say that the mishna [means that] even after the fact it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:17:1.hebrew: פסח עצמו כשר - קס"ד לזרוק דמו ולהקטיר חלבו, אבל לאכילה לא, וקתני: ואדם יוצא בו ידי חובתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:17:1.english: The Paschal lamb itself is valid - It was initially assumed [that this means it is valid] to sprinkle its blood and burn its fat, but not for eating; and [yet the baraita] teaches: "and one fulfills his obligation with it."

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:17:2.hebrew: ור' נתן היא - דאמר אכילה לא מעכבא, ולא בעי ר' נתן גברא דחזי לאכילה. ומתניתא קמייתא מוקי ר' אלעזר כרבנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:17:2.english: And it is Rabbi Natan - For he says eating is not essential, and Rabbi Natan does not require a person who is fit for eating. And the first baraita, Rabbi Elazar establishes in accordance with the Rabbis.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:18:1.hebrew: אין מחשבת אוכלין - חולה וזקן בזריקת דם, דאיש לפי אכלו לגבי שחיטה כתיב:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:18:1.english: There is no [disqualifying] intent regarding eaters - [i.e.,] a sick person or an elderly person, during the sprinkling of the blood, because "every man according to his eating" is written with regard to the slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:19:2.hebrew: גברא דחזי לאכילה בעי' - דכי כתיב "איש לפי אכלו", אגברא כתיב, דליהוי גברא בר אכילה, אבל פסח לא איכפת לן אי לא חזי:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:19:2.english: We require a person who is fit for eating - For when [the verse] "Every man according to his eating" is written, it is written regarding the person — that the person must be capable of eating — but [regarding] the Paschal lamb, it does not matter to us if it is not fit [to be eaten].

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:20:1.english: It should be sprinkled in purity - With [ritually] pure priests and service vessels.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:21:1.hebrew: ור' נתן היא - דאמר אכילה לא מעכבא, ולא בעי ר' נתן גברא דחזי לאכילה. ומתניתא קמייתא מוקי ר' אלעזר כרבנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:21:1.english: And it is Rabbi Natan - Who says eating is not essential, and Rabbi Natan does not require a person who is fit for eating. And Rabbi Elazar establishes the first baraita in accordance with the Rabbis.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:21:2.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן בציבור - שנטמאו רוב ציבור בין שחיטה לזריקה, כגון שמת הנשיא ונטמאו. הילכך, גברי דחזו לאכילה נינהו:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:21:2.english: With what are we dealing here? With [the] public - [Meaning] that the majority of the public became ritually impure between the slaughter [of the Paschal lamb] and the sprinkling [of its blood], for example, that the Nasi died and they became impure. Therefore, they are men who are fit for eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:22:1.english: A decree lest - in another year, the public will become impure after [the] sprinkling [of the blood].

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:22:2.hebrew: ויאמרו אשתקד - מי לא היינו טמאין בשעת אכילה ואכלנו, ואע"פ ששחיטתו בטהרה? השתא נמי, אע"פ ששחיטתו וזריקתו בטהרה, ניכול בשר בטומאה! ולא ידעי דאשתקד בעידנא דהוי זריקת הדם טמאין הוו, והוה ליה פסח הבא בטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:22:2.english: And they will say: Last year - Were we not impure at the time of eating and [yet] we ate, even though its slaughter was in [a state of] purity? Now too, even though its slaughter and sprinkling were in [a state of] purity, let us eat the meat in [a state of] impurity! And they do not know that last year, at the time of the sprinkling of the blood, they were [already] impure, so it was a Paschal offering that came in [a state of] impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:2:1.hebrew: אלא - תרווייהו ביחיד, והא לכתחלה והא דיעבד. והא דקתני "אם זרק הורצה" ואוקימנא ביחיד — ה"מ דמודה רבי יהושע בדיעבד כשנטמא, דהא עלה קאי, ומשום דאיתיה בעינא; אבל באבוד ושרוף — לא. ור' יוסי אפילו נשרפו או אבדו שיריה קאמר, אם הקטיר קומצה — כשירה:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:2:1.english: Rather - Both of them [refer to] an individual [offering], and this one [is] ab initio and that one [is] after the fact. And [as for] that which it teaches, "If he sprinkled [the blood], it was accepted," which we established [as referring to] an individual [offering] — this applies [only] where Rabbi Yehoshua concedes after the fact when [it] became impure, for it is regarding that [case] that he is speaking, and because it is [still] in existence; but where [it was] lost or burned, [he does] not [concede]. Whereas Rabbi Yosei states [this] even [if] its remainders were burned or lost: if he burned its handful [of flour on the altar], it is valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:4:1.hebrew: נטמא בשר וחלב קיים אין זורק את הדם - אפי' לר' אליעזר, דעיקר פסח לאכילת אדם קאתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:4:1.english: [If] the meat became ritually impure and the fat remains [pure], one does not sprinkle the blood - Even according to Rabbi Eliezer, because the primary [purpose of] the Paschal offering is for human consumption.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:4:2.hebrew: ובמוקדשין אינו כן - אפילו לר' יהושע, שאפילו נטמא בשר וחלב קיים — זורק את הדם, דהא תרתי איכא: מתיר ושיריים, שהדם מתיר אימורין למזבח:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:4:2.english: And with [other] consecrated offerings it is not so - Even according to Rabbi Yehoshua, [for] even if [the] meat became impure and [the] fat remains [pure], one sprinkles the blood, since here there are two [components]: a permitting agent and a remainder, as the blood permits the sacrificial portions for the altar.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:5:1.english: It was accepted - And [he] is exempt from observing the second Pesach.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:5:2.english: Does not preclude - atonement after the fact.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:8:1.english: Those who eat - A sick person and an elderly person.

Rashi on Pesachim 78b:9:1.hebrew: רב - דאית ליה אכילת פסחים לא מעכבא, דאמר כר' נתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 78b:9:1.english: Rav - Who holds [that] eating of the Paschal offerings is not indispensable, as he stated [his view] in accordance with Rabbi Natan.

Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:11:1.hebrew: שאני התם דאי מימשכי הני כו' - תימה לרשב"א: והא בשעת זריקה אינם יכולים לימשך, ונמצא דהשתא לא חזי לאכילה? וי"ל דדילמא ר' נתן סבר כר"ש, דתנן לקמן בפרק האשה (פסחים דף פט.): "נמנין ומושכין ידיהם עד שיזרק הדם". אי נמי: נטמאו מקצתן או שמתו, חזי להני:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:11:1.english: It is different there, as if these withdraw, etc. - This is astonishing to Rashba: But at the time of sprinkling [the blood], they cannot withdraw, and thus it turns out that now it is not fit for eating? And one can say that perhaps Rabbi Natan holds like Rabbi Shimon, as we learned in a Mishnah later in chapter HaIshah (Pesachim 89a): "People may register [for a Pesach offering] and withdraw their hands [from it] until the blood is sprinkled." Alternatively: if some of them became ritually impure or died, it is fit for these [remaining registrants].

Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:16:1.hebrew: ולרבי נתן איש לפי אכלו למה לי דבעינן גברא דחזי לאכילה - וא"ת: לרבנן נמי לישני הכי לעיל כי פריך "ולעכב לא?", לימא: כי אתא קרא לעכב — היינו דבעינן גברא חזי לאכילה, אבל בשר לא. ולאו פירכא היא, דרבנן בעו בשר חזי לאכילה, כדתניא לעיל: "אחרונים שאין להם כזית אינם אוכלין, וחייבין לעשות פסח שני". והא נמי לא תיקשי: אמאי לא משני לר' נתן "איש לפי אכלו" למצוה, כדבעי למימר לעיל? משום דלא אשכחן תנא דלא מקיש אוכלין למנויין אלא זקני דרום לחודייהו בפרק שני דזבחים (דף כג.). ולמאי דמוקי מתני' כר' נתן, צ"ל ד"יוצאין בפסח אחד" דקאמר, היינו דוקא דיעבד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:16:1.english: "And according to Rabbi Natan, why do I [need] 'according to every man's eating'? Because we require a person who is fit for eating" - And if you ask: According to the Rabbis too, let [the Gemara] answer thus above when it asks "And is it not essential?" — let it say: when the verse comes to make it essential, that means we require a person fit for eating, but not meat! [However,] this is not a difficulty, because the Rabbis require meat that is fit for eating, as it was taught in a Baraita above: "The last ones, who do not have an olive's bulk, do not eat [it] and are obligated to observe the Second Pesach." And this too should not be difficult: why does [the Gemara] not answer that according to Rabbi Natan, "according to every man's eating" is [only] for the optimal fulfillment of the mitzvah, as it wanted to say above? Because we do not find a Tanna who does not compare eaters to registrants except the Elders of the South alone, in the second chapter of Zevachim (23a). And according to the one who establishes the Mishnah like Rabbi Natan, one must say that when it says "they fulfill their obligation with one Pesach offering," that is specifically after the fact:

Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:17:1.hebrew: לימא ר' נתן היא כו' - תימה לר"י, והיכי מיתוקמא כר' נתן? והא ר' נתן ורבנן לא פליגי אלא בבשר, אבל בגברא לכ"ע בעינן גברא דחזי לאכילה! ועוד, א"כ אפילו שחטו שלא לאוכליו נמי, ואמאי נקט "שחטו לאוכליו"? ועוד, היכי תיסק אדעתיה למימר השתא דיש מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה? הא פשוט בכולי גמרא דאין מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה, כדמוכח בזבחים (דף ד.) ובתמיד נשחט לעיל (דס"ח.), ושם הבאתי. ונראה לר"י דה"פ: "נזרק דמו שלא לאוכליו" — לא שנזרק שלא לשם אוכליו, אלא שבשעת זריקה היו הבעלים חולים. והשתא קאמר: כמאן? כר' נתן. דמשמע ליה, כיון דר' נתן מיקל כולי האי ולא בעי שיהא בשר ראוי לאכילה, ה"נ לא חייש אם אין בעלים ראויין בשעת זריקה; אבל רבנן דמחמרי ובעו שיהא בשר ראוי לאכילה, ה"ה דבעו שיהו הבעלים ראויים לאכילה בשעת זריקה. וה"נ סבר ר' אלעזר בסמוך, דלא בעי ר' נתן גברא חזי אלא בשחיטה דווקא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:17:1.english: Let us say it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Natan, etc. - This is astonishing to the Ri: how can it be established in accordance with Rabbi Natan? For Rabbi Natan and the Rabbis only disagree regarding the meat, whereas regarding the person, according to everyone we require a person who is fit for eating! Furthermore, if so, even if he slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it [it should] also [be valid], so why did [the baraita] state "slaughtered it for those who can eat it"? And furthermore, how could it enter [the Gemara's] mind to say now that there is an intention regarding eaters during the sprinkling [of the blood]? Why, it is obvious throughout the entire Gemara that there is no [disqualifying] intention regarding eaters during the sprinkling, as is proven in Zevachim (4a) and in [chapter] Tamid Nishchat above (68a), and I have cited [it] there. And it appears to the Ri that this is its explanation: "[and] its blood was sprinkled for those who cannot eat it" — not that it was sprinkled with an intention not for eaters, rather that at the time of sprinkling the owners were sick. And now [the Gemara] says: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Natan. For it seemed to [the Gemara] that since Rabbi Natan is so lenient and does not require that the meat be fit for eating, so too he is not concerned if the owners are not fit [to eat] at the time of sprinkling; whereas the Rabbis, who are stringent and require that the meat be fit for eating, likewise require that the owners be fit for eating at the time of sprinkling. And so too Rabbi Elazar holds immediately below, that Rabbi Natan only requires a person fit [to eat] specifically at the time of slaughtering.

Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:2:1.hebrew: הא אמרת מודה רבי יהושע בציבור - תימה לרשב"א: מאי קושיא? דילמא ה"ק: "רואה אני דברי רבי אליעזר בציבור, שאף ר' יהושע לא אמר אלא ביחיד", דכי האי גוונא אמרי' פ"ק דחולין (דף יב.) ובכמה דוכתי. ואומר ר"י דהכא לא שייך למימר הכי, דלא קתני בברייתא לא בציבור ולא ביחיד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:2:1.english: "Didn't you say [that] Rabbi Yehoshua concedes regarding a communal [offering]" - Rashba is perplexed: What is the difficulty? Perhaps this is what [Rabbi Yosei] means: "I see as correct the statement of Rabbi Eliezer regarding a communal [offering], for even Rabbi Yehoshua only stated [his dissenting view] regarding an individual [offering]," as we say in this manner in the first chapter of Chullin (12a) and in several places. And Ri says that here it is not applicable to say so, since neither "regarding a communal [offering]" nor "regarding an individual [offering]" is taught in the baraita.

Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:3:1.english: When [Rabbi Yehoshua] concedes regarding [a case where the meat] became impure - [That is] because the tzitz [High Priest's headplate] effects acceptance.

Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:7:1.hebrew: ולעכב לא והתניא במכסת נפשות - תימה לר"י: והא קרא בשחיטה כתיב, ומהתם נפקא דמחשבת אוכלין פסלה בשחיטה, אבל בזריקה אמרן לעיל דאין מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה, והיכי פריך משחיטה אזריקה? ואומר ר"י: דווקא מחשבת אוכלין ליתא בזריקה אלא בשחיטה, אבל כשאין לו אוכלין לגמרי אף בשעת זריקה, סברא היא דפסול, שהיא עיקר עבודה, כיון דבשעת שחיטה הקפיד הכתוב אפילו אמחשבה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 78b:7:1.english: "And [was it] not [stated] to preclude? Wasn't it taught [in a baraita]: According to the number of souls" - It is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzchak: isn't the verse written regarding slaughter, and from there it is derived that an [improper] intention regarding eaters disqualifies during slaughter, whereas regarding sprinkling [of the blood] we said above that [improper] intention regarding eaters does not apply to sprinkling — so how does [the Gemara] raise an objection against [the law of] sprinkling from [a verse about] slaughter? And Rabbi Yitzchak says: specifically [improper] intention regarding eaters does not apply to sprinkling, only to slaughter; however, when it has no eaters at all even at the time of sprinkling, it is logical that it is disqualified, since [sprinkling] is the primary service, given that at the time of slaughter Scripture was strict even regarding intention.
